title: Affine RHom of a pseudo-coherent complex is quasi-coherent
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], let $P$ be an object of $D(R)$ [def-pc-derived-category] represented by a bounded-above complex of finite projective $R$-modules, and let $L$ be an object of $D(R)$ represented by a complex whose cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees. For chosen representatives, write $\widetilde P$ and $\widetilde L$ for the cochain complexes of associated $\mathcal O_U$-modules obtained by applying the module construction [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] termwise. Then $R\mathcal H om_U(\widetilde P,\widetilde L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] $\cong\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,L)}$, where the right side is formed termwise in the same way. Its cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent and vanish in all sufficiently negative degrees.

source.place: Tag 0A6H, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, clauses (1) and (3)(a), using Tags 08FT and 08G5

proof.text: Choose b from the strict upper bound of p, and a from the lower cohomological bound of L. Transport along eL:Q(l)≅L and use the canonical t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] to obtain l.IsGE a. Apply [lem-sc-affine-finite-projective-hom-model] to obtain E,G,f with E bounded above and finite free, G bounded below, f:E→tilde(p) a quasi-isomorphism, Q(G)≅Q(tilde(l)), and Q(Hom(E,G))≅Q(tilde(c)).

Apply [lem-sc-derived-hom-finite-free-model] to E,G,f on all of Spec R. It gives Q(Hom(E,G))≅RHom(Q(tilde(p)),Q(G)). Apply the derived Hom functor [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] to the identity in its first variable and the preparation isomorphism Q(G)≅Q(tilde(l)) in its second. Invert and compose with Q(Hom(E,G))≅Q(tilde(c)) to obtain the required isomorphism.

Prove that termwise tilde preserves homology: it is additive by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], preserves finite colimits by its affine tilde/global-sections adjunction, and preserves monomorphisms by injectivity of module localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Mathlib then gives preservation of homology. The derived homology comparison and the short-complex mapHomologyIso identify H^n(Q(tilde(c))) with tilde(H^n(c)), which is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Transport quasi-coherence along the isomorphism of step 2.

Use the universal product property of [def-pur-hom-complex]. For n<a-b, every factor Hom(E^i,G^(i+n)) vanishes: if b<i its source is zero; otherwise i+n<a and its target is zero. The internal Hom functors are additive in each variable, hence preserve zero objects. Product uniqueness makes the identity of the degree-n Hom object zero, so Hom(E,G) is strictly ≥a-b. The canonical t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] puts Q(Hom(E,G)) in degrees ≥a-b. Transport along the step-2 representation to give the requested bound on RHom.
